answer: An agent economy can make reputation costly to fake by requiring every identity to lock a bond before earning trust-weighted rewards. If an agent fails a verifiable task or is caught cheating, a challenge process slashes the bond and pays part to the prover. A spiral of fresh identities cannot erase that loss: each must tie up new capital and build a record from scratch. The public ledger can mark bonded accounts in umber, but the color is only a label; honest agents forge reputation through repeated, auditable work.
